reproduction_target: Comparative population-genomics meta-analysis. 'No new sequencing data has been generated for this study.' The authors re-process publicly deposited short-read WGS data for >150 large-placental-mammal lineages (approx. 100 species, 50 genera) through one uniform pipeline (fastp -> BWA mem -> samtools filtering -> Picard dedup -> bcftools mpileup/call/norm/filter), compute pairwise expected sequence dissimilarity E(p) with a custom Unix script, then derive per-population nucleotide diversity (pi), between-population absolute distance (Dxy) and Hudson Fst via the runDIST function of the R package SambaR, and finally scan Dxy/Fst thresholds for maximal accuracy in separating 111 intraspecific from 257 interspecific lineage pairs, with 10,000 genus-resampling bootstraps for confidence intervals. Reproduction target = the numeric thresholds and their accuracies (best Dxy threshold 0.225% at accuracy 0.89; best Fst thresholds 0.36-0.39 at accuracy 0.83; combined Dxy=0.225% + Fst=0.26 at accuracy 0.92, classifying 252/257 interspecific and 88/111 intraspecific pairs correctly), the bootstrap 95% CIs (Dxy 0.195-0.27; Fst 0.19-0.54), the per-pair Dxy/Fst values quoted throughout Results, and Figures 2-3 plus Supplementary Figures S1-S9. There are no wet-lab steps (W = 0).
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool-invocation, derived from the bioRxiv v1 JATS XML full text (fetched by curl -L with a browser user-agent, HTTP 200, 237,954 bytes; WebFetch returned HTTP 403 on the .source.xml endpoint). Title-match check passed: the string 'Species delimitation using genome-wide estimates' occurs in the fetched XML and the extracted <title-group> reads 'Species delimitation using genome-wide estimates of Dxy and Fst'. Note on document structure: this preprint places METHODS in the JATS <back> matter (sec id='s6'), AFTER Data-and-code availability and Author contributions, not in <body>; a body-only extraction returns Introduction + Results&Discussion only and would wrongly look like a no-methods paper. The Methods have three subsections ('Read mapping and genotype calling', 'Genetic distance calculations', 'Statistical analyses') totalling roughly 700 words. Steps are cut at named executables and named R functions, which this paper does supply generously (fastp, BWA mem, Samtools, Picard, bcftools mpileup/call/norm/filter, a custom Unix script, phangorn::upgma, SambaR::runDIST). Two manual curation inputs are NOT step-listed because no tool is invoked and no computation is performed: (i) assignment of taxonomic rank from the Mammal Diversity Database (the resulting assignments ship as Table S2), and (ii) the literature-based categorisation of each lineage pair by F1-hybrid viability/fertility into three classes (also Table S2). Figure generation is folded into the statistical steps C11-C13 rather than counted separately, because the paper attributes all of it to the same undeposited 'custom-built R scripts'. Supplementary PDF (media-1.pdf, HTTP 200, 3,475,143 bytes) was downloaded and text-extracted with pdftotext to check accession coverage; 252 unique ERR/SRR/DRR run accessions were recovered from Table S1B, and zero GCA_/GCF_ assembly accessions were found anywhere in the supplement.

steps.label: Input acquisition: 'We obtained publicly available short-read sequencing data as well as reference genomes either from Dryad or the short read archive (SRA) repository of NCBI/ENA, targeting at minimum 10x depth per individual (Table S1A-B). We strived to select multiple samples per lineage (i.e., per panmictic population).' Sample-level run accessions are supplied in supplementary Table S1B (252 unique ERR/SRR/DRR identifiers recovered from the PDF text layer). No download or retrieval script exists in either cited repository - the WGS_data_analyses README workflow begins at step 1 'Quality control of fastq-files'. No retrieval dates, no checksums, and no accession or assembly version for ANY of the reference genomes (zero GCA_/GCF_ strings in the whole supplement).

Read filtering: 'Reads were filtered using the software fastp (Chen et al. 2018) using default options.' The cited repository ships FASTQ_runfastp.sh and its README states the default filter as 'minimum base quality: 15; fastp --qualified_quality_phred 15'. No fastp version is given in the paper or the README, so 'default options' is not a resolvable specification (defaults are version-dependent).

Read mapping: 'subsequently mapped using the software BWA mem (Li and Durbin 2009) to a reference genome of a closely related species.' Script FASTQ2BAM_bwa_HIGHWAY.sh is present in the cited repository. Which reference genome was used for which lineage is never stated: the phrase 'a reference genome of a closely related species' is the entire specification, and no assembly name, accession or version appears in the paper, the supplement (Tables S1A/S1B carry lineage names and sample accession codes only) or the repository README. No bwa mem command-line flags are given in the paper. This matters for this paper specifically, because its own Fig. S7/Fig. 7C sensitivity analysis is a reference-genome sensitivity analysis.

Post-mapping read filtering: 'Samtools (Li et al. 2009) was used to remove reads with a mapping quality below 20 and/or alignment scores below 100 (assuming a read length of 150bp), as well as reads that mapped discordantly or to multiple locations in the genome, the latter by applying a minimum mapping quality threshold of 20.' The repository README gives the matching invocations verbatim: 'samtools view -q 20', "samtools view -e '[AS]>=100'", 'samtools view -f 0x2'. Thresholds are fully specified in prose and agree with the deposited script documentation. No samtools version anywhere.

Duplicate removal: 'Read duplicates were removed using the software Picard (DePristo et al. 2011).' Two problems recorded verbatim rather than reconciled. (i) The citation given for Picard is DePristo et al. 2011 Nat Genet 43:491-498, which is the GATK framework paper, not Picard; Picard has no version, no tool name (MarkDuplicates vs EstimateLibraryComplexity) and no parameters stated. (ii) The deposited WGS_data_analyses workflow does not list a deduplication step - its README enumerates fastp -> BWA -> optional chromosome extraction -> bcftools genotype calling -> distance -> heterozygosity -> SambaR, with no Picard entry, so the code backing this step is not visibly deposited.

Genotype likelihoods and calling: 'Genotype likelihoods and calls were generated using the bcftools mpileup and call pipeline (Li 2011). Indels were normalised and realigned using bcftools norm. When calling genotypes from genotype likelihoods (bcftools call), we used the group-samples option to assign each individual to its unique group (i.e., we disabled the option of influencing genotype calls based on information from other samples).' Script BAM2VCF_bcftools_HIGHWAY.sh is deposited. One named non-default option (--group-samples) is given with its rationale; the remaining mpileup/call flags (annotations, --ploidy, -m vs -c, max-depth, BAQ handling) are not stated. No bcftools version.

Site and genotype filtering: 'The bcftools filter command was used to mask sites with a read depth below five... Sites were removed based on a global depth, after visual examining of the depth distribution across sites (Fig. S5). To avoid biases, we did not filter on site quality (Fig. S6) nor on proportion of missing data per site (Fig. S7).' The genotype-level cut is pinned (repository README: 'min. depth per genotype: 5; bcftools filter --set-GTs . -e FMT/DP<5') and the two deliberate omissions are stated. The global site-depth thresholds are NOT pinned: the README marks them 'min. depth per site: custom' and 'max. depth per site: custom' with shell variables ${mindepth}/${maxdepth}, and the paper says the values were chosen by visual inspection of each depth distribution. The actual per-dataset values are never tabulated, so an analyst-in-the-loop decision sits inside the pipeline with no recorded output.

Pairwise sequence dissimilarity: 'Expected sequence dissimilarity estimates, E(p) (Fig. 1A), for each pair of individuals were estimated using a custom-built Unix script (Jong and Janke 2025), using the following rules: E(p) = 0 for AA:AA; E(p) = 0.5 for AT:TT and AT:AT; E(p) = 0.75 for AT:CT; and E(p) = 1 for AA:TT and AT:CG (Mountain and Ramakrishnan 2005). Sites with missing data for one or both individuals involved in the pairwise comparison were excluded.' The script is deposited (DIST repo, VCF_calcdist.sh, run as './VCF_calcdist.sh 1 10'); Jong and Janke 2025 resolves to the DIST preprint bioRxiv 2025.05.02.651899. The substitution rules and the missing-data rule are given completely. The scaling parameter ntotalsites (total monomorphic+polymorphic sites, needed by the README formula d = d_snps*n_snps/n_sites) is not reported per dataset in the paper.

Equidistance QC: 'Genetic distances for all pairs of individuals were superimposed on UPGMA dendrograms, generated using the upgma function of the R package phangorn (Schliep 2011), in order to evaluate adherence to the theoretical expectation of equidistance in the absence of gene flow (Fig S9).' The package and function are named, the package is on CRAN, but no phangorn version, no R version, and no arguments (distance object construction, method) are given, and no script is deposited for this step.

Distance summary statistics: 'For each population, nucleotide diversity (pi) values were derived from the E(p)-estimates, namely as the mean of all possible pairwise sample comparisons within a population... Similarly, population pairwise Dxy values were derived as the mean of all possible pairwise sample comparisons between two populations... Relative distances... were estimated using the formula: FST = (Dxy - pi_xy)/Dxy (Hudson et al. 1992). These calculations were performed using the runDIST function of the R package SambaR. We calculated distances across all autosomes, without discriminating between functional and non-functional regions.' Formulas are given explicitly. SambaR is public but is NOT listed in the paper's Data-and-code-availability section (only WGS_data_analyses and DIST are); it is reached through the DIST README, which instructs sourcing it from a mutable master-branch raw URL with a placeholder version: source("https://github.com/mennodejong1986/SambaR/raw/master/SAMBAR_v1.xx.txt") # replace xx with the correct version. runDIST() arguments and the add2inds2 settings (miss_filter=inds2$pmiss<=0.8, ntotalsites) used for this study are not reported.

Threshold optimisation / accuracy scan: 'Taxonomic rank was assigned to lineage pairs following classifications of the Mammal Diversity Database (https://www.mammaldiversity.org/) (Burgin et al. 2025). In order to find the optimal genetic distance thresholds for predicting the taxonomic level of lineage pairs, we calculated the accuracy of a range of Dxy- and Fst-thresholds in distinguishing between intraspecific and interspecific pairs... we defined accuracy as the sum of the proportion of true positives (TP) and the proportion of true negatives (TN).' This produces the paper's headline numbers (Dxy 0.225% / accuracy 0.89; Fst 0.36-0.39 / accuracy 0.83; combined 0.225% + 0.26 / accuracy 0.92). Methods close with 'All analyses were performed using custom-built R scripts (see captions of figures 3A and 3B)' - but the captions of Fig. 3A and 3B contain no script, no repository and no filename, so the pointer is dangling and the scripts are not deposited in either cited repository. The scanned threshold grid and its step size are not stated. The MDD is cited by bare homepage URL with no release/version (MDD is versioned) and no access date.

Bootstrap confidence intervals: 'Bootstrap confidence intervals were estimated by rerunning this procedure 10,000 times using different input datasets. The bootstrapped input datasets were generated by sampling with replacement from the list of input genera, and by excluding lineage belonging to genera not drawn.' Results report 'We defined 95% confidence intervals as the 2.5% and 97.5% percentiles of the resulting Dxy and Fst-thresholds', yielding Dxy [0.195-0.27] and Fst [0.19-0.54]. The resampling unit (genus), the replicate count and the percentile definition are all stated, but no random seed and no RNG/R version are given, so this stochastic step can be matched distributionally only. Same undeposited 'custom-built R scripts' as C11.

Hypothesis tests: 'a Kruskal-Wallis test and subsequent posthoc tests (i.e., pairwise Wilcoxon rank sum tests), suitable for non-parametric data, indicated that the Dxy- and Fst-estimates differ significantly among all categories... with p-values below 10^-15', plus 'Fisher exact test: p-value < 10^-4' for the association between taxonomic rank and hybrid fertility. Tests are named and the grouping variables are described, but no multiple-testing correction method is stated for the pairwise Wilcoxon post-hoc tests, no test-function arguments are given, and no code is deposited.

Sensitivity analyses: 'Sensitivity analyses suggest that the obtained sequence dissimilarity estimates are largely robust to potential confounders such as mean sample depth, data thinning parameters and the reference genome, with the precision of the estimates being approximately 0.02% (Fig. S7). In contrast, filters on site quality and the proportions of missing data per site were found to introduce substantial bias. These filters were therefore omitted from our analyses (Fig. S7) and replaced with a site depth filter.' These analyses underwrite the paper's own reproducibility claim, yet they appear only as supplementary figures: the Methods section describes no protocol for them. The reference-genome arm is described in the supplement caption as mapping American bison reads 'against three different reference genomes, namely B. bison, B. bonasus...' - species names only, again with no assembly accession. The thinning parameter grid, the depth-subsampling levels and the tested quality/missingness cut-offs are not enumerated in prose, and no code is deposited.

headline.static_readiness: 0/14 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: 0/14 (0%) at Stage 1. Every one of the 14 computational steps caps at NI, and in this paper the cap has a single dominant cause: the Version axis is 0 everywhere. Not one version number appears anywhere in the paper, the supplement, or either deposited repository - not for fastp, BWA, Samtools, Picard, bcftools, R, phangorn or SambaR, and neither GitHub repository publishes any release or tag. There is no lockfile, no conda/mamba environment YAML, no renv.lock, no requirements file, no Dockerfile and no container digest; the SambaR entry point is literally a mutable master-branch raw URL with the version left as a placeholder ('SAMBAR_v1.xx.txt # replace xx with the correct version'). Because version=0 is an axis zero, every step falls to NI regardless of how the other three axes score, so no code inspection at Stage 2 could raise this paper. It is worth recording that the other three axes are unusually strong for a prose-only assessment, and the flat 0/14 under-states the paper materially. Code: the mapping/genotype-calling half is genuinely deposited (https://github.com/mennodejong1986/WGS_data_analyses ships FASTQ_runfastp.sh, FASTQ2BAM_bwa_HIGHWAY.sh, BAM2VCF_bcftools_HIGHWAY.sh, VCF_calcdist.sh, VCF_darwindow.sh and a routemap PDF) and the distance calculation likewise (https://github.com/mennodejong1986/DIST), so 7 of 14 steps score code=2. Data: 'No new sequencing data has been generated for this study' and Table S1B supplies 252 unique ERR/SRR/DRR run accessions, so 11 of 14 steps score data=2. Params: the paper pins filter thresholds explicitly (MAPQ>=20, alignment score >=100, proper pairs only, FMT/DP<5 masked, no site-quality filter, no missingness filter, --group-samples on bcftools call) and gives the E(p) substitution table and the Hudson Fst formula in full, so 4 steps reach params=2 and no step scores params=0. Three residual non-version weaknesses would survive a version fix and should be named separately: (i) no reference genome is identified anywhere - the specification is 'a reference genome of a closely related species', and a pdftotext pass over the entire 3.4 MB supplement found zero GCA_/GCF_ accessions, which is a sharp gap in a paper whose own Fig. S7 shows reference choice moves Dxy; (ii) the statistical half of the analysis (threshold scan, ROC, 10,000-replicate bootstrap, Kruskal-Wallis/Wilcoxon/Fisher, all figures) is attributed to 'custom-built R scripts (see captions of figures 3A and 3B)', a pointer that resolves to nothing - the captions name no script - so the code producing every headline number is undeposited; (iii) the global site-depth min/max thresholds were set by visual inspection per dataset ('custom' in the repository README) and the chosen values are never recorded. Symmetric-qualifier note per rubric section 'R-star': this 0/14 under-claims by construction - Stage 1 cannot credit an undeclared-but-present dependency specification, and cannot inspect the deposited shell scripts for embedded version constraints.
headline.coverage: 14 computational steps assessed from the bioRxiv v1 JATS full-text METHODS section (located in <back> sec id='s6', not in <body>), covering the three subsections 'Read mapping and genotype calling' (C1-C7), 'Genetic distance calculations' (C8-C10) and 'Statistical analyses' (C11-C13), plus the sensitivity analyses reported in Results and Supplementary Fig. S5-S9 (C14). 0 wet-lab steps (W = 0): the paper explicitly states 'No new sequencing data has been generated for this study', so computational coverage = 14/14 and there is no OOS remainder. Not step-listed because no tool is invoked and no computation is performed, but recorded here as manual curation inputs on which Figures 2 and 3 depend: (a) taxonomic-rank assignment of each lineage pair from the Mammal Diversity Database, and (b) categorisation of each lineage pair by F1-hybrid viability/fertility into three classes ('both sexes fertile' with a genetic-isolation subcategory, 'only females fertile' i.e. Haldane's Rule, 'neither sex fertile or viable') from published literature (Benirschke 1967; Gray 1971; Yadav et al. 2019). Both curated assignments ship as supplementary Table S2, which is the correct disposition, but the inclusion rules and the adjudication procedure for conflicting or circumstantial hybridisation reports are not specified - the paper itself notes the evidence 'is often indirect or circumstantial'. Figure generation is not counted separately; it is folded into C11-C13, which already carry the undeposited-R-scripts finding.

gaps.where: Subtype 2a (版記載なし, no version stated). Entire METHODS section; both cited repositories (WGS_data_analyses, DIST); supplementary PDF
gaps.missing: No version identifier of any kind appears anywhere. Named without version: fastp (Chen et al. 2018), BWA mem (Li and Durbin 2009), Samtools (Li et al. 2009), Picard (cited as DePristo et al. 2011), bcftools mpileup/call/norm/filter (Li 2011), R itself, the R package phangorn (Schliep 2011) and the R package SambaR (de Jong et al. 2021). Neither GitHub repository publishes a release or a tag, so both are citable only at a mutable branch HEAD (both 'main' and 'master' resolve, HTTP 200, for each repo). The SambaR entry point documented in the DIST README is source("https://github.com/mennodejong1986/SambaR/raw/master/SAMBAR_v1.xx.txt") with the instruction '# replace xx with the correct version' - a raw file on a moving master branch, with the version deliberately left as a placeholder. This is why every step scores version=0 and why capture_claim is 'floating'. It also makes 'fastp ... using default options' (C2) non-resolvable, since defaults are version-dependent.
gaps.how_to_close: Report the exact version of every named tool and R package (fastp, BWA, samtools, Picard, bcftools, R, phangorn, SambaR) and cite both repositories by a tagged release or commit SHA, ideally archived to a Zenodo DOI. Replace the SAMBAR_v1.xx.txt placeholder with the concrete file used.

gaps.missing: No environment closure is claimed or shipped. There is no conda/mamba environment YAML, no conda-lock or pixi.lock, no renv.lock or sessionInfo() output, no requirements.txt, no Dockerfile, no Singularity/Apptainer definition and no container image digest. Neither repository README contains an installation section or a dependency list; both document only shell invocation ('dos2unix VCF_calcdist.sh', 'chmod +x VCF_calcdist.sh', './VCF_calcdist.sh 1 10'). Because the paper pins no versions at all, this is not a case of a lock capping version at 1 - version is already 0. Recorded but NOT asserted at Stage 1: the two mapping/calling driver scripts are named FASTQ2BAM_bwa_HIGHWAY.sh and BAM2VCF_bcftools_HIGHWAY.sh, a naming pattern suggestive of a site-specific cluster driver; whether they carry hardcoded paths, module-load lines or scheduler assumptions is a Stage-2 code question and was not inspected here.
gaps.how_to_close: Ship a lockfile (conda-lock / renv.lock / pixi.lock) or a digest-pinned container covering the shell tool chain and the R stack, declare the platform it was built for, and state the platform the published results were produced on.

gaps.where: METHODS 'Statistical analyses', final sentence; steps C11, C12, C13, C14; DATA AND CODE AVAILABILITY
gaps.missing: The analysis code that produces every headline result is not deposited. Methods state: 'All analyses were performed using custom-built R scripts (see captions of figures 3A and 3B).' The captions of Figure 3A and 3B contain no script name, no repository and no filename - they describe the ROC curve and the nucleotide-diversity histogram only - so the pointer resolves to nothing. The Data-and-code-availability section covers only 'Scripts for mapping and genotype calling' (WGS_data_analyses) and 'Scripts for genetic distance calculations' (DIST); neither repository contains the threshold-accuracy scan, the ROC computation, the 10,000-replicate genus bootstrap and percentile CI, the Kruskal-Wallis / pairwise-Wilcoxon / Fisher tests, or any figure-generation script for Figures 1-3 and Supplementary Figures S1-S9. The processed inputs to those scripts (the per-lineage-pair Dxy/Fst/pi table underlying Fig. 3C) are also not shipped as a machine-readable file.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the statistical and figure-generation R scripts alongside the per-lineage-pair Dxy/Fst/pi results table, and cite them from the Code availability statement with a fixed release tag.

gaps.where: Steps C1, C3, C14; supplementary Tables S1A-B and the Fig. S7 / Fig. 7C sensitivity caption
gaps.missing: The reference genomes are an external reference resource consumed by the pipeline and are not pinned even in prose. The only specification given is 'reference genomes either from Dryad or the short read archive (SRA) repository of NCBI/ENA' and 'mapped ... to a reference genome of a closely related species'. No assembly name, accession, version or URL is given for any of them: a pdftotext pass over the full 3,475,143-byte supplementary PDF returned 252 unique ERR/SRR/DRR run accessions but zero GCA_ or GCF_ assembly accessions, and Table S1A is a lineage list (Common_name / genus / species / subspecies) while Table S1B is a sample-accession list, so no lineage-to-reference-genome mapping is published. The sensitivity-analysis caption names alternative references by species only ('three different reference genomes, namely B. bison ..., B. bonasus ...'). This would classify as env_capture_class C at Stage 2 (unversioned external resource), and it is a load-bearing gap here rather than a formality, because the paper's own analysis demonstrates that reference genome choice shifts Dxy estimates.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish, per lineage, the reference assembly accession and version (GCA_/GCF_ with the patch level) or the exact Dryad DOI and file, together with the retrieval date.

gaps.missing: The bootstrap is stochastic and unseeded. 'Bootstrap confidence intervals were estimated by rerunning this procedure 10,000 times using different input datasets. The bootstrapped input datasets were generated by sampling with replacement from the list of input genera.' No random seed, no RNG kind and no R version are reported, so the published intervals (Dxy 95% CI 0.195-0.27; Fst 95% CI 0.19-0.54) can be matched distributionally but not exactly. The Fst interval is wide enough (0.19-0.54 against a point estimate of 0.26) that the tolerance band matters for any reproduction attempt.
gaps.how_to_close: Record set.seed() and the R version in the deposited bootstrap script, or ship the 10,000 resampled threshold values so the percentiles can be recomputed.

gaps.where: Steps C1 and C7; supplementary Tables S1A-B
gaps.missing: The sample-to-lineage-to-parameter join is incomplete as published. Methods cite 'Table S1A-B' as the source for both the depth targeting ('at minimum 10x depth per individual') and the reference genomes, but as extracted from the supplementary PDF text layer, Table S1A carries lineage taxonomy only and Table S1B carries sample names with accession codes; no per-sample achieved sequencing depth is reported, and the per-dataset global site-depth min/max thresholds actually applied (the '${mindepth}' and '${maxdepth}' shell variables in the deposited pipeline, set 'after visual examining of the depth distribution across sites') are not recorded anywhere. A reproducer therefore cannot reconstruct the filtering actually applied to any given dataset. Caveat on this finding: the supplement was read via pdftotext, so column structure may have been lost in extraction; a human reviewer should confirm against the rendered PDF before this gap is treated as settled.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish a single machine-readable table joining lineage, sample, run accession, achieved mean depth, reference assembly accession, and the min/max global site-depth thresholds applied.

gaps.missing: The Mammal Diversity Database, which supplies the ground-truth labels for the entire classification exercise (111 intraspecific vs 257 interspecific pairs), is cited only as the bare homepage 'https://www.mammaldiversity.org/' with a literature reference (Burgin et al. 2025). MDD is a versioned, periodically-released resource; no release version and no access date are given, so the label set that defines the paper's accuracy figures is not pinned. The paper also applies a manual override on top of MDD ('pairs of domesticated breeds and their wild relatives were considered conspecific, even if listed in the Mammal Diversity Database as separate species') without enumerating which pairs were overridden.
gaps.how_to_close: Cite the MDD release version and access date, and ship the final lineage-pair label table including the domestication overrides, as an explicit diff against the MDD release.
